Article In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by: Region is Bengkalis Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Government of Bengkalis Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Bengkalis.
Regional Apparatus is the Regional Apparatus of Bengkalis Regency as a supporting element of the Regent and Regional
4.
House of Representatives in the administration of governmental affairs that are the authority of the Region. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen)
5.
years, including a child still in the womb. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties, either temporarily or based on court determination.

7.
Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred.
Child protection is all activities to guarantee
8.
and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence.
Violence is any act that is unlawful, with or without the use of means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body, or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.
9.
Violence against women is any action
10.
based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 12.

13.
suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion, or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household.
Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
14.
Guardian is a person or body that in fact exercises parental authority as a Parent over a Child.
15.
Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father
16.
and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. Society is individuals, families, groups, and/or community organizations.
17.

18.
who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, milk kinship, foster care, and representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household. 19. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or
20.
indirectly as a result of violence that occurs in the Bengkalis Regency area. 21.

22.

23.

24.

Assistance is an effort made by a person or

26.

Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to
27.
physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to be able to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society.

28.
who experiences social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
29.

Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to conduct the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against
30.
women and children that is gender responsive.

children and women at the Sub-district and Village/Kelurahan level.
35.

36. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer or receipt of a person by threat of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited.
37. Empowerment is a process of developing independence and welfare of a person or community by increasing knowledge and skills to meet their life needs both economically and socially. 38. Article 12
Other violence as referred to in Article letter constitutes threat of violence and coercion.
(1) Threat of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) includes every unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause (2) fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom. Coercion as referred to in paragraph (1) includes a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something that is contrary to their own (3) will.

Second Part
Implementation of Protection for Women and Children from Acts of Violence

Article 11
Exploitation as referred to in Article letter includes: acts of economic or sexual exploitation with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
a.
acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced work or
b.
services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, physical exploitation, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or capabilities of a person by other parties to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and/or all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, but not limited to prostitution activities or sexual abuse.

CHAPTER VII CRIMINAL PROVISIONS
Article 45
Every person who intentionally commits violence against women and children as referred to in Article up to Article 12 shall be subject to criminal sanctions as regulated in laws and regulations.

Second Part
Implementation of Protection for Women and Children from Acts of Violence

Article 19
Parents, guardians and/or family members legally have (1) full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence, report when violence occurs and protect victims. Parents and/or family members must carry out prevention (2) of all forms of violence by providing guidance and example in accordance with religious teachings and applicable norms. In the event that parents, guardians and/or family members as referred to in paragraph (1) do not exist or their whereabouts are unknown or due to a certain reason cannot carry out their obligations and responsibilities, then (3) the obligations and responsibilities may be transferred to the Regional Government and other family members implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER COOPERATION AND PARTNERSHIP
Part One
Cooperation

Article 41
In order to achieve the objectives of protection of women and children as referred to in Article 4, Regional Governments may cooperate with other parties in accordance with (1) the provisions of laws and regulations.
The cooperation as referred to in paragraph (1) includes: (2)
a. exchange of data and information;
b. rehabilitation of victims of violence;
c. repatriation and social reintegration; and
d. provision of evidence and witnesses.
The cooperation as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (3) (2) shall be set forth in the form of a Joint Agreement and/or Cooperation Agreement in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 10
Neglect as referred to in Article letter includes: a. acts that result in the failure to fulfill the needs of a child properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care; b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after a child as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
c. acts of deliberately neglecting women and children within the household sphere, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to agreement or contract they are obligated to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to such women; and/or
d. acts that result in economic dependence by means of restricting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of such person.

b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or authorized parties; and c. participating in the handling of victims of acts of violence.

Article 10
Neglect as referred to in Article letter includes: a. acts that result in the failure to fulfill the needs of a child properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care; b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after a child as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
c. acts of deliberately neglecting women and children within the household sphere, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to agreement or contract they are obligated to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to such women; and/or
d. acts that result in economic dependence by means of restricting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of such person.

Article 19
Parents, guardians and/or family members legally have (1) full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence, report when violence occurs and protect victims. Article 20
(1) The community has the obligation and responsibility for the protection of women and children victims of violence through community participation activities in the protection of women and children.

a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children;
b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or authorized parties; and c. participating in the handling of victims of acts of violence.

Article 20
(1) The community has the obligation and responsibility for the protection of women and children victims of violence through community participation activities in the protection of women and children.
(2) Forms of community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children;
b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or authorized parties; and c. participating in the handling of victims of acts of violence.

Article 19
Parents, guardians and/or family members legally have (1) full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence, report when violence occurs and protect victims. Parents and/or family members must carry out prevention (2) of all forms of violence by providing guidance and example in accordance with religious teachings and applicable norms. In the event that parents, guardians and/or family members as referred to in paragraph (1) do not exist or their whereabouts are unknown or due to a certain reason cannot carry out their obligations and responsibilities, then (3) the obligations and responsibilities may be transferred to the Regional Government and other family members implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
